## Use in Wildfires

- Classification: `adapted` code and shaders plus two `verbatim` planet cubemap textures.
- Purpose: Genesis 3x2 square-planet face order, static cube geometry, center-star directional surface lighting, ray-box atmosphere rendering, the upstream Earth/Moon cubemaps used to preserve the intended surface art and seam contract, and its separation of authoritative level transfer from a bounded client transition screen.
- Partition root: `src/main/java/first/wildfires/thirdparty/genesisadapt/`, `NtmAscentPlanetRenderer.java`, the return-capsule transition classes/packet/Mixin listed in `files.csv`, the vehicle-first ordering contribution to the dual-derived `ReturnCapsuleService.java`, plus `src/main/resources/assets/wildfires/shaders/core/genesis_planet_*`.
- ARR dependency direction: the Wildfires orbit renderer calls this Apache-2.0 partition; the partition has no VS2, Lodestone, Genesis runtime or physical-ship dependency.
- Modifications: ported to Forge `RegisterShadersEvent` and static `VertexBuffer`; removed VS2/VantagePoint/Lodestone and the upstream ship-shadow dependency; made planet alpha compatible with NTM distance LOD and independent Wildfires orbital-cloud tint/alpha; removed forced `gl_FragDepth=1.0`; restored the exact upstream per-face winding/UV orientation and cube-corner lighting gradient; and adapted the cube atmosphere to Forge GLSL 150 with encoded local entry coordinates, ray-box/diagonal-plane limb evaluation, Genesis path-normalized entry/exit illumination, center-star lighting, and datapack-controlled day/sunset/night palettes, regional brightness, terminator transitions, limb response, opacity and exposure. Wildfires additionally extends both adapted shaders with a bounded four-caster, fixed 3x3 finite-square-star visibility pass: rotating satellite OBBs are intersected from the actual three-dimensional cube surface/shell position so geometric umbra and penumbra cross face edges and corners without UV seams; atmosphere eclipses attenuate direct scattering while retaining ambient/night scattering. Orbit-wide sky colour remains exclusively NTM black; the Genesis atmosphere is only a local cube shell. Cubic cloud-shell geometry remains rigidly aligned to the planet. The bound-surface ascent pass now prefers the current dimension's registered provider and otherwise reuses the cached common-universe ephemeris; its Genesis surface and atmosphere receive the Sun-to-selected-body vector rather than an Earth-only vector. Its reveal boundary is the exact camera-ray exit from the rotated outermost cube shell, including the configured cloud and atmosphere radii, so no Genesis body layer is submitted while the camera remains inside it. The transition partition captures the last live NTM-style capsule flight frame before the entity/passenger level hand-off, acknowledges the exact source ticket only after that capture completes on the client thread, substitutes the capture for Minecraft's receiving-level screen at `Minecraft.setScreen` entry, keeps the transition active across screen `removed/onClose`, and reveals the prepared target scene only after the service-side same-UUID tracking/remount acknowledgement and two actual destination render frames. For orbit arrival, the authoritative station context is now sent before Respawn and a destination frame counts only when the current body's Genesis square surface was actually drawn; black vacuum, absent context/state, point LOD and unavailable shaders cannot satisfy the barrier. As soon as that exact target passenger graph and square-body frame are proven, the receiving screen stops covering the live target framebuffer while the final server commit completes, so a successfully rendered Earth cannot remain hidden behind the older departure capture. The high-version server transfer also adapts Genesis' target-vehicle-first order: `addDuringTeleport` the reconstructed capsule before player Respawn/teleport, then reattach the player. On the client, only the exact target dimension and capsule UUID may repair the local passenger graph, with motion/fall frozen until server confirmation. The earlier synthetic `ReturnCapsuleTransitionOverlay` was removed; `ReturnCapsuleReceivingScreen` is now the sole transition presentation and never calls the vanilla loading-screen renderer. It retains no Genesis registry, ship, OBB, scale or VS2 type.
- Transition passenger-graph refinement (2026-08-14): after target-vehicle-first teleport, the client barrier now requires the `LocalPlayer` to reference the exact capsule object currently tracked in the destination level and the capsule passenger list to reference that same player. It permits vanilla `SetPassengers` to eject the pre-Respawn graph and may detach only a removed or wrong-level same-UUID capsule before retrying the exact target; unrelated live vehicles remain protected. Bounded status diagnostics expose the current vehicle, target passenger count and repair result without per-frame log spam.
- Shader-binding cost refinement (2026-08-14): each Genesis shader registration callback now constructs an immutable binding object containing that exact `ShaderInstance` and all fixed surface, atmosphere and four-slot satellite-shadow uniforms. Orbit and surface-ascent passes reuse those handles instead of repeating named lookups and indexed-name construction each frame. Resource reload still replaces the complete binding generation atomically; missing names retain Minecraft's no-op `AbstractUniform` behavior, and uniform write order, values, pass order, geometry, textures, shadows and rendered pixels are unchanged.
- Transition framebuffer lifecycle refinement (2026-08-15): normal completed trips continue reusing one same-size departure capture to avoid repeated GPU allocation, while an exact abort or client-world logout now clears ownership first and explicitly destroys the retained colour/depth attachments. Off-render-thread cleanup captures the old target before queuing destruction, so a later render callback cannot destroy a newly allocated transition frame.
- Surface-transition shadow continuity (2026-08-15): the Genesis-derived square surface, rigid cloud shell and atmosphere shell used under the reusable capsule now receive the same four-caster finite-square-star visibility frame as ordinary orbit rendering. The receiver's rendered Minecraft size may follow the bounded transfer profile, while caster geometry stays normalized to the selected body's synchronized physical radius; this preserves the same geometric umbra/penumbra across different body sizes and through ascent/re-entry without adding an FBO or shadow map.
- Surface-transition render-state isolation (2026-08-15): the dual-derived `NtmAscentPlanetRenderer` now restores depth testing, depth writes, back-face culling and ordinary blending after its Forge `AFTER_SKY` square surface/cloud/atmosphere pass. Genesis pixels, mesh orientation, atmosphere and shadow uniforms are unchanged; the isolation only prevents the pass from corrupting later chunk, reusable-pod and passenger geometry during ascent or re-entry.
- Verbatim resources: `textures/planets/minecraft/overworld.png` and `textures/planets/genesis/moon.png`, redistributed byte-for-byte under the recorded Apache-2.0 project terms; their exact hashes and destinations are in `files.csv`.
- Full source is shipped in this repository. The JAR includes this record and `upstream/LICENSE`.
- Dual-derived targets: `ReturnCapsuleService.java` is primarily an NTM Space LGPL-3.0-only adaptation and is also listed in the NTM manifest. Genesis contributes the Forge 1.20.1 vehicle-first transfer ordering under Apache-2.0. `NtmAscentPlanetRenderer.java` combines NTM's underfoot-body altitude contract with Genesis' cube mesh/surface/atmosphere presentation and retains both notices. Both destinations remain listed in every applicable manifest and are not mislabelled as Apache-only.
